description:
*Own the coffees PPP buys, the profiles we roast and the releases we bring to cafés, retail and wholesale customers. This is a hands-on specialty roastery role based in Singapore.*

*Report to the Head of Operations. Work with the production roasting partner on trials and with PPP’s trainer on routine cupping and outlet calibration.*

**Key Responsibilities**

**A. Green sourcing & purchasing**

* Write buying briefs for core blends and seasonal single origins.
* Sample-roast and blind-cup lots. Document selection and rejection decisions.
* Compare landed cost, availability, crop timing and supplier terms.
* Recommend purchase quantities against demand, stock cover and cash budget.

**B. Roast development & quality**

* Develop and document target profiles for espresso and filter coffees.
* Run production trials with the roasting partner and evaluate batch consistency.
* Set sensory references, tolerances and release criteria.
* Investigate failed batches and agree corrections before release.

**C. Coffee programme**

* Own a rolling 12-month blend and single-origin calendar.
* Plan substitutions ahead of crop changes and stock depletion.
* Define each coffee’s intended cup, channel and price position.
* Brief training, retail and wholesale teams before launch.

**D. Commercial performance**

* Cost saleable roasted kilos including green loss, toll fees and packaging.
* Review margins, sell-through and stock age by coffee.
* Reconcile forecast purchases against actual usage.
* Escalate supply or cost risks with a workable alternative.

**E. Partner handover**

* Maintain approved profiles, batch records and reference samples.
* Calibrate the production partner against PPP’s cup standards.
* Give the training lead practical references for routine QC.
* Own escalation when routine QC falls outside the approved profile.

**Requirements:**

* Hands-on experience in a specialty coffee roastery, including sample roasting and production profile development.
* Experience selecting green lots and recommending purchases against a budget.
* Ability to describe a coffee release you personally owned, from sample evaluation to launch.
* Working knowledge of roast yield, costing and inventory planning.
* Confidence giving a production partner specific corrective feedback.
* Experience tasting espresso and filter coffees across roast levels.
* Ability to translate sensory results into clear buying and release decisions.
* Comfort working with cafés and wholesale teams.

**NOTE: Please include your CV, one coffee you sourced or profiled, your role in its release, expected salary and earliest start date in your application, thank you.**

title: Global Operations Key Account Manager

description:
CEVA Logistics provides global supply chain solutions to connect people, products, and providers all around the world. Present in more than 170 countries and with over 110,000 employees across 1,500 sites, we are proud to be a Top 5 global 3PL.
  
  
Every day, our people imagine better ways to serve a world in motion – creating smarter, safer, and more sustainable solutions for our customers.
  
  
YOUR ROLE
  
  
We are seeking an experienced Global Operations Key Account Manager to lead the worldwide operational relationship with one of our strategically important global technology customers.
  
  
Based in Singapore, you will take ownership of operational performance and customer experience across our Air & Ocean business, working closely with senior customer stakeholders and CEVA teams throughout Asia Pacific, Europe and North America.
  
  
This is a highly visible, customer-facing role requiring strong international freight forwarding expertise, commercial awareness and the ability to influence operational performance across a complex global network. You will play a key role in strengthening customer relationships, driving service excellence and supporting the long-term retention and growth of the account.
  
  
WHAT ARE YOU GOING TO DO?
  
  
**Specifically, you will:**  
Own and coordinate the global operational relationship for an assigned strategic customer across Air & Ocean, ensuring consistent service delivery against agreed commitments.
  
  
Act as a senior operational contact for customer stakeholders, managing escalations and driving effective resolution of complex service issues across multiple countries.
  
  
Monitor global service performance against agreed KPIs and SLAs, identifying performance gaps and coordinating root-cause analysis and corrective actions with regional and country teams.
  
  
Lead global monthly and quarterly business reviews (MBRs/QBRs), providing meaningful performance insights, improvement plans and recommendations to senior customer stakeholders.
  
  
Partner with Global Key Account Management, Business Development, Product and Operations teams to support account strategies, customer retention and business growth.
  
  
Establish, maintain and improve customer Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), ensuring consistent application of agreed processes and service standards across the global network.
  
  
Coordinate the operational implementation and onboarding of new business, trade lanes and service requirements, working closely with regional implementation and operations teams.
  
  
Identify and lead continuous improvement initiatives, including process optimisation, automation, digital reporting and opportunities to improve service quality and cost efficiency.
  
  
Guide and influence regional and local operational teams to ensure accountability, effective collaboration and a consistent customer experience across markets.
  
  
WHAT ARE WE LOOKING FOR?
  
  
You are an accomplished international freight forwarding and operational account management professional who combines strong customer relationship management with the ability to drive service performance across global operations.
  
  
You are comfortable engaging senior customer stakeholders, navigating complex operational challenges and influencing teams across different markets, cultures and time zones.
  
  
**You will also have:**  
Extensive experience in international freight forwarding or logistics, with strong operational knowledge of both Air and Ocean products, supported by a bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification.
  
  
Demonstrated experience managing complex strategic customer accounts at regional or global level, including senior stakeholder engagement, operational governance and service recovery.
  
  
Strong analytical and problem-solving capability, with experience managing service KPIs, SLAs, root-cause analysis, business reviews and continuous improvement initiatives.
  
  
Excellent communication, influencing and relationship management skills, with the ability to lead cross-functional teams and drive outcomes within a global matrix organisation.
  
  
Advanced Microsoft Excel and presentation skills, with exposure to business intelligence tools such as Power BI or Tableau highly regarded.
  
  
Experience supporting global technology, semiconductor or other complex multinational supply chains would be advantageous.
  
  
The successful candidate will require flexibility to engage with stakeholders across global time zones, including occasional meetings outside standard Singapore business hours.
  
  
WHAT DO WE HAVE TO OFFER?
  
  
In addition to a challenging and rewarding work environment and competitive compensation, we are proud to offer a range of employee benefits designed to support your wellbeing, and help you thrive at work and in life.
  
  
**Personal wellbeing:** benefit from comprehensive group insurance and medical coverage, including Group Term Life, Personal Accident, Hospital & Surgical, Major Medical, outpatient GP and Specialist benefits. Eligible dependants are also covered under the Hospital & Surgical and Major Medical plans.
  
  
**Work-life balance:** enjoy 19 working days’ annual leave in your first year, increasing progressively with service, together with applicable medical, hospitalisation, marriage, childcare, compassionate and palliative care leave.
  
  
**Flexible benefits:** receive SGD 1,000 per year in flexible benefits, which may be used across eligible medical, dental, optical, health and wellness, personal development and selected lifestyle expenses.
  
  
**Professional development:** your growth is essential to us. Unlock your potential through internal mobility opportunities, leadership and mentoring programmes, and MyLearning – our global online platform with more than 1,000 courses.
  
  
Diversity is core to who we are.
  
  
By reflecting the cultures and perspectives of our customers and communities, we perform at our best. CEVA Logistics is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from all qualified candidates.

title: CEO
company: South Central Community Family Service Centre
description:
**Role Summary:**  
As Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of South Central Community Family Service Centre (SCC), reporting to the Board of Directors, you will lead an organisation dedicated to “Poverty Transformation With-in Empowered Communities”. This is an extraordinary opportunity to shape the future of a vibrant, mission-driven organisation delivering critical services in areas such as social work interventions, Home Ownership, Livelihood, and Child Learning & Development programmes.
  
  
You will inspire and lead a passionate team, foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, and excellence, and drive digital transformation and evidence-informed practice to ensure services make a tangible difference for families. The CEO will also champion organisational sustainability, strengthen partnerships with government, funders, and the community, and elevate SCC as a thought leader in the social service sector. The role is focused on strategy, growth, partnerships, and sector influence, with day-to-day operations led by the senior management team.
  
  
As CEO, you will set the strategic direction for SCC’s flagship KeyStart Home Ownership Programme and its complementary Livelihood and Fresh Start Support Programmes, growing their reach and impact through partnerships with government, funders, and the community, so that more families in public rental housing achieve home ownership and social mobility. You will lead a senior management team that includes the Director, Clinical and Community Practice, and other senior roles.
  
  
If you are a values-led, visionary leader who thrives at the intersection of strategy, impact, and people, this role offers a platform to create lasting change for families and communities, leaving a legacy that extends far beyond the organisation itself.
  
  
Key Accountabilities
  
  
1. Strategic and Organisational Leadership
  
  

* Drive Strategic Direction: Lead the formulation of SCC’s strategic plan and key policies, partnering with the Board to secure its endorsement, and drive their execution to advance SCC’s mission and ensure long-term sustainability. Provide strategic advice to the Board on organisational priorities, emerging risks, and sector developments.
* Anticipate and Shape the Future: Track shifts in policy, funding, and community needs, and identify new areas for SCC to grow its impact, including new services, partnerships, and locations.
* Strengthen Organisational Capability: Build a future-ready organisation by designing and scaling the systems, structures, and processes that enable SCC to deliver high-quality, integrated services and achieve measurable outcomes for families and children.
* Lead and Develop People: Lead and develop the senior management team and, through them, all staff, fostering a professional, ethical, and values-driven organisational culture.
* Organisational Design: Shape SCC’s structure and senior leadership team, appoint and develop senior leaders, and ensure succession plans are in place for key roles.
* Champion Organisational Culture: Shape and role-model a culture of collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement, building an engaged, high-performing workforce that lives SCC’s mission and values.

2. Accountability to Board & Governance
  
  

* Work closely with the Board to chart the vision and strategies to fulfil its mission.
* Provide timely, accurate, and relevant information to enable effective Board oversight and informed decision-making.
* Ensure compliance with the Charities Act, Code of Governance for Charities and IPCs, and SCC’s internal policies.
* Recommend to the Board the necessary and appropriate human resource requirements for effective execution of the work.
* Work closely with Board Sub-Committees and the Senior Management Team, and provide regular updates on organisational progress, needs and issues.

3. Service Innovation and Impact
  
  

* Set the direction for SCC’s services and programmes, developing new and integrated service models that strengthen family stability and resilience across Home Ownership, Livelihood, and Child Learning & Development.
* Hold the senior management team accountable for meeting MSF, NCSS, and funder service standards, KPIs, and reporting requirements, including outcomes relating to housing stability, economic self-reliance, and child development.
* Promote outcome-based practice, service integration, and continuous improvement across the organisation to achieve holistic and measurable improvements in family and child well-being.
* Use evidence from research and evaluation to scale what works, adapt or stop what does not, and position SCC’s practice models for adoption across the sector.

4. Strategic Leadership of the Home Ownership & Livelihood (HOLI) Vertical
  
  

* Leads the strategic direction, planning, and execution of the Home Ownership and Livelihood verticals, ensuring alignment with SCC’s mission of poverty transformation and integration across internal and external ecosystems.
* Grows the reach and impact of HOLI programmes by securing partnerships, funding, and policy support, and by refining programme models based on evidence and cost-effectiveness.
* Ensures day-to-day delivery of HOLI programmes is led by HOLI programme lead, with clear accountability for quality, outcomes, reporting, and compliance.

5. Fundraising, Resource Development and Financial Sustainability
  
  

* Provide financial leadership and oversight, holding the senior management team accountable for budget performance, and present the annual budget to the Board for approval, with day-to-day financial management, controls, and audits
* Strengthen organisational sustainability through funding diversification and effective grants management.
* Work closely with the Board and funders to drive fundraising and financial sustainability for non-funded initiatives, including identifying, developing, and securing funding streams across all verticals through proposals, institutional grants, and donor partnerships.
* Personally cultivate relationships with major donors, foundations, and corporate partners, and lead SCC’s most significant funding requests.

6. Oversight of Shared Services
  
  

* Provide strategic direction to the Shared Services team, covering finance, human resources, information technology, corporate services, partnership and Research, Evaluation and Development (RED).
* Ensure SCC maintains sound internal controls, enterprise risk management, data protection, and business continuity in line with the Code of Governance for Charities and IPCs, and report on these to the Board.

7. Government Relations, Partnerships and Sector Influence
  
  

* Serve as SCC’s chief spokesperson and build trusted relationships with government agencies, funders, and community partners.
* Develop strategic partnerships with government, corporate, academic, and community organisations to co-create solutions and extend SCC’s reach.
* Build SCC’s brand and public profile, leading its communications strategy and media engagement.
* Advocate for the needs of families and communities served by SCC, consistent with Board-approved positions.
* Drive sector-level thought leadership and contribute to SCC’s participation in national social service transformation efforts, including areas of housing stability, social mobility, and livelihood development.
* Build networks across the social service sector, and represent SCC on sector platforms, committees, and collaborations.

Qualifications and Experience
  
  

* Degree in a relevant discipline, or equivalent experience; postgraduate qualification preferred.
* At least 10 years of senior leadership experience, preferably in the social service, non-profit, or public sector.
* Track record of setting strategy and leading organisational growth or transformation, with sound financial and governance judgement.
* Strong understanding of the Singapore social service and charity governance landscape.
* Experience in strategic planning, service model development, and cross-sector collaboration in the social services; familiarity with housing, livelihood, and social mobility is an advantage.
* Proven track record in fundraising and diversifying funding sources.
* Experience leading digital transformation or the use of data to improve services.
* Established networks across government, the social service sector, and funders, with experience in advocacy or public engagement.
* A values-led leader with the integrity, resilience, and credibility to lead both frontline and corporate teams.

ABOUT US
  
  
Who We Are
  
  
Formerly known as Bukit Ho Swee Family Service Centre, South Central Community Family Service Centre (SCC) provides support to the low-income and vulnerable families in our community. While giving support to families who seek help in financial, social or relationship issues, we encourage community self-help and cooperation.
  
  
At SCC we believe that
  
  

* Everything is possible when we use our strengths as people living in the neighbourhood.
* We can become a community of people who are resources to one another.
* We receive from others when we are in need, and we give back when others are in need.
* This community can be a place where there is mutual support, encouragement, and self-help.

Our Approach
  
  
Taking an inclusive approach, we leverage on the community to activate mutual help through social connections and inclusiveness with the aim of empowering the low-income and vulnerable families while developing the full potential of the next generation for transformative change.

title: Associate Director - Automation
description:
**Job Title:** Associate Director - Automation
  
  
**About Singapore ADC Site:**  
Be part of history in the making. AstraZeneca is building its first biologics manufacturing campus in Singapore — a groundbreaking USD 1.5 billion investment that will serve as a global hub for innovation and excellence.
  
  
This innovative facility will deliver end-to-end Antibody-Drug Conjugate (ADC) capabilities with different manufacturing units/buildings in one campus:
  
  
Small molecule- chemical API production
  
  
Large molecule- monoclonal antibody manufacturing
  
  
Conjugation
  
  
Fill-and-finish operations, including sterile filling and lyophilization
  
  
Final secondary packaging
  
  
The campus will be equipped with innovative digital and automation infrastructure, enabling autonomous manufacturing powered by artificial intelligence. In addition, it will be designed for carbon neutrality, embedding sustainability into every aspect of operations and setting a new benchmark for environmentally responsible biologic's manufacturing.
  
  
**Introduction to role:**  
Are you ready to lead automation that accelerates safe, reliable medicines to patients and brings a smart factory vision to life? This role connects strategy to execution, turning digital ambition into operational reality across a complex manufacturing environment.
  
  
You will set the direction for Operational Technology and automation, guide high-impact projects from concept to qualification, and build a culture where engineers thrive. Working closely with multi-functional partners, you will ensure our plants are ready for tomorrow’s demands—more medicines, delivered faster and more affordably—while safeguarding quality and compliance. How will you shape our OT landscape to unlock autonomous manufacturing and measurable performance gains?
  
  
**Accountabilities:**  
**OT Strategy and Architecture:** Provide guidance into the development of engineering approaches and OT strategy, ensuring systems are specified and delivered in alignment with AstraZeneca’s global automation strategy and the broader Engineering framework.
  
  
**Program Leadership and Delivery:** Manage planning, budgeting, solution development, supplier liaison and contract management to deliver projects that achieve operational readiness and sustained performance in operations.
  
  
**Stake-holder Collaboration:** Collaborate with Global Engineering and Site Engineering to drive successful project execution and readiness; work with Global IT to align data standards and infrastructure that enable autonomous manufacturing and smart factory technologies.
  
  
**Technical Authority and Critical issue:** Act as a technical advisor to senior management and an escalation point for complex issues; develop fit-for-purpose engineering delivery solutions aligned to global and local priorities.
  
  
**Performance and Cost Management:** Control and monitor cost, capacity planning and utilization to operate within budget; own and drive critical metrics across productivity, quality, safety, schedule adherence and cost.
  
  
**Standards and Compliance:** Develop standards that achieve technical excellence, right-first-time outcomes and regulatory compliance; participate in FDA audits and other inspections, supporting audit readiness and automation-related responses.
  
  
**Validation Leadership:** Lead and execute FAT/SAT/IQ/OQ/PQ activities end-to-end, including planning, coordination, documentation review, test execution, deviation resolution and final closure.
  
  
**Expansion and Change Enablement:** Support and deliver in-house expansion projects involving automation scope; support the business in communicating and enabling change across the area.
  
  
**Digital, Data and AI Enablement:** Use approved AI tools and digital capabilities to improve work efficiency, support analysis, enhance documentation workflows and strengthen problem-solving effectiveness; develop or support automation dashboards and reporting to increase visibility of system performance, alarms, trends and operational insights.
  
  
**Supplier and Contract Management:** Manage supplier performance and maintain contracts that secure reliable, high-quality engineering services for projects and operations.
  
  
**People Leadership and Culture:** Coach automation engineers and own development plans; create an inclusive, collaborative culture, own grey areas across functions and drive best-in-class outcomes with diverse teams.
  
  
**Continuous Improvement and Sustainability:** Drive a Continuous Improvement mind-set that delivers lean, cost-efficient operations and supports environmental sustainability goals.
  
  
**Documentation and Governance:** Maintain technical-documentation in line with internal procedures and regulatory requirements, including system records, specifications, test documents and change documentation.
  
  
**Essential Skills/Experience:**  
Degree in Engineering
  
  
Leadership experience in manufacturing, engineering, and project management
  
  
Capability in developing and implementing business strategy
  
  
Project and change-management skills
  
  
Leadership experience in managing teams
  
  
Comprehensive understanding of lean operations
  
  
Experience and comfort in dealing with ambiguity
  
  
Full and detailed knowledge of relevant Safety, Health & Environment legislation
  
  
Proven domain expertise in SCADA/PLC and DCS
  
  
Deep knowledge in IT/OT architecture and OT cybersecurity
  
  
**Desirable Skills/Experience:**  
Post-graduate Engineering or business qualification
  
  
Implementation of Digital / autonomous roadmap
  
  
Facility startup and ops preparation
  
  
Knowledge in cGMP regulations and regulatory agency expectations
  
  
When we put unexpected teams in the same room, we unleash bold thinking with the power to inspire life-changing medicines. In-person working gives us the platform we need to connect, work at pace and challenge perceptions. That's why we work, on average, a minimum of three days per week from the office. But that doesn't mean we're not flexible. We balance the expectation of being in the office while respecting individual flexibility. Join us in our unique and ambitious world.
  
  
**Why AstraZeneca:**  
Here, your engineering leadership directly shapes how life-changing medicines reach patients with speed, quality and reliability. You will work at the intersection of cutting-edge automation, data, and validation with cross-discipline teams who combine curiosity with disciplined delivery. We invest in modern manufacturing, digitalisation and sustainability, bringing unexpected teams together to solve complex problems and scale what works. You will find a culture that values kindness alongside ambition, where you can lead, learn and leave a tangible legacy—advancing smart factory capabilities while helping reduce our environmental footprint.
  
  
When we put unexpected teams in the same room, we unleash bold thinking with the power to inspire life-changing medicines. In-person working gives us the platform we need to connect, work at pace and challenge perceptions. That's why we work, on average, a minimum of three days per week from the office. But that doesn't mean we're not flexible. We balance the expectation of being in the office while respecting individual flexibility. Join us in our unique and ambitious world
  
  
**Call to Action:**  
Step into this opportunity to lead automation that delivers measurable outcomes for patients and the business—take the next move to build, scale and inspire the future of manufacturing excellence.

title: Senior Assistant Manager, Learning Systems & Digital Innovation
description:
Family Group: Administration

* **JOB PURPOSE**

The Senior Assistant Manager, Learning Systems & Digital Innovation supports the Chief, People & Organisation Development (P&OD) and Deputy Director by:

* Overseeing institutional oversight of WH’s learning systems, digital learning resources and related HRIS learning processes, including the integrated NHG Health learning platform (LENS), SAP SuccessFactors (iConnect), e-journal resources and organisation-wide subscription platforms.

* Ensuring the reliability, governance, effective use and continuous improvement of learning systems that support the delivery, assignment, tracking and reporting of staff learning.

* Partnering internal stakeholders, NHG system owners, vendors and cross-institution workgroups to translate operational requirements into system enhancements, process improvements and sustainable digital solutions.

* Identifying and implementing opportunities to improve P&OD processes through technology, robotic process automation, workflow automation and data analytics.

* Supporting effective departmental operations, governance and resource stewardship, including acting as the responsible party for P&OD’s fixed assets.

* **MAJOR DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES**

*Specific*

  

* Learning Systems Management and Service Continuity

* Institutional learning-systems oversight

* Serve as WH’s institutional lead and primary point of coordination for learning systems and related HRIS learning processes, including LENS and iConnect.
* Oversee the day-to-day operation, administration and service management of learning-system processes to support reliable business-as-usual operations.
* Maintain appropriate institutional configurations, access arrangements, user roles and administrative controls in accordance with prevailing policies and system-governance requirements.
* Establish and maintain clear operating procedures, service workflows, escalation routes, user guides and knowledge resources.
* Monitor system issues, service requests and recurring user difficulties, ensuring appropriate investigation, escalation and closure.
* Coordinate incident response and business-continuity arrangements when learning systems or critical functions are unavailable.
* Maintain an appropriate issue, risk and decision log for significant system matters.
* Escalate material operational, data, cybersecurity or service-continuity risks to the relevant system owners and P&OD leadership.
  

* Learning data, records and reporting

* Oversee the integrity, completeness and appropriate use of learning-system data and records.
* Partner programme owners (such as Nursing Education, Clinical departments, Allied Health teams, etc) and other stakeholders to ensure that mandatory and operationally critical learning is appropriately configured, assigned, tracked and reported.
* Coordinate investigations and remediation where learning records, enrolments, completions, interfaces or reports are incomplete or inaccurate.
* Develop and maintain operational dashboards and management reports on system utilisation, learning completion, service issues, user adoption and other relevant indicators.
* Support audit, compliance and management-reporting requirements relating to learning systems and records.
* Work with relevant stakeholders to define data requirements, validation rules, reporting logic and appropriate access controls.
  

* Learning Systems Lifecycle Management, Enhancement & Adoption

* Manage the ongoing lifecycle of WH’s learning systems and related digital platforms, from operationalisation and adoption through enhancement, optimisation and eventual transition or replacement.
* Represent WH in relevant NHG and cross-institution learning-system workgroups, ensuring WH’s operational requirements, user needs and implementation considerations are appropriately represented.
* Partner internal stakeholders, including but not limited to Nursing Education, Clinical Services, Allied Health and programme owners, to understand learning-system requirements and translate these into appropriate system configurations, enhancements or process solutions.
* Gather, assess and prioritise business requirements and coordinate enhancement requests with NHG system owners, IT teams and vendors.
* Coordinate impact assessments, user acceptance testing, implementation readiness and post-implementation reviews for new releases, functionalities, integrations and system changes.
* Plan and coordinate institutional readiness and user-adoption activities when new functionality or significant system changes are introduced.
* Develop or coordinate user communications, briefings, guides, clinics and capability-building interventions for course owners, administrators and other system users.
* Monitor system utilisation, adoption, recurring issues and user feedback to identify opportunities for system and process improvement.
* Ensure learning-system changes are appropriately governed, tested, documented and transitioned into business-as-usual operations.
  

* Digital Learning Resources and Subscription Platforms

* Oversee the organisation-wide administration and governance of e-journals, databases, digital knowledge resources and subscription platforms supporting clinical and professional practice.
* Manage subscription renewals, access arrangements, licence administration, usage information, vendor coordination and stakeholder communications.
* Partner clinical departments and other users to review resource requirements, utilisation and service issues.
* Maintain an accurate inventory of digital-resource subscriptions, contractual periods, users, costs and renewal timelines.
* Coordinate access troubleshooting and resolution with vendors, internal users and relevant technical teams.
* Review usage and cost data to support renewal, consolidation, rationalisation and resource-allocation decisions.
* Support procurement, quotation, contracting, invoicing and budget-monitoring processes relating to subscription platforms.
* Ensure continuity of access to approved resources and timely communication of material changes to stakeholders.
* Maintain appropriate documentation and controls to support audit, financial governance and regulatory requirements.
  

* Digital Innovation, Process Improvement and Analytics

* Process discovery and innovation

* Partner P&OD workstream owners to identify recurring manual activity, duplication, bottlenecks, control gaps and opportunities for service improvement.
* Map current and future-state processes and recommend practical improvements across people, process, technology and data.
* Facilitate requirements-gathering sessions with users and translate operational needs into clear process or solution specifications.
* Assess proposed improvements based on user impact, feasibility, risk, controls, effort and expected benefits.
* Develop implementation plans, measures of success and post-implementation review arrangements.
* Maintain a prioritised pipeline of P&OD digitalisation and process-improvement opportunities.
  

* Automation and RPA

* Identify suitable use cases for workflow automation, robotic process automation and low-code solutions within P&OD.
* Develop or coordinate the development of appropriately governed solutions using approved enterprise tools, where relevant. These may include Microsoft Power Automate, Power Apps, SharePoint, Microsoft Forms and approved RPA platforms.
* Apply automation selectively to stable, rules-based and repetitive processes, while retaining human review for exceptions, approvals, judgement-based decisions and sensitive cases.
* Coordinate solution design, testing, deployment, documentation, access controls and handover to process owners.
* Monitor automation performance, failure points and user adoption and coordinate timely remediation.
* Ensure that automated workflows have clear ownership, exception-handling arrangements and business-continuity procedures.
  

* Technology and analytics

* Develop fit-for-purpose dashboards and analyses that improve visibility of learning operations, system use, service performance and process outcomes.
* Partner process owners to define meaningful indicators, data sources, calculation rules and reporting frequencies.
* Conduct trend, volume, turnaround-time, exception and utilisation analyses to identify operational risks and improvement opportunities.
* Support the use of approved analytics tools, such as Microsoft Excel and Power BI, for management reporting and operational decision-making.
* Evaluate emerging technologies and recommend appropriate pilots or adoption opportunities, considering business value, usability, integration, cybersecurity, data protection and sustainability.
* Document measurable outcomes from digital initiatives, including time saved, reduction in manual handling, improvement in data quality, faster turnaround time or better user experience.
  

* Governance, Risk, Compliance and Documentation

* Develop, implement and periodically review policies, guidelines, work instructions, standard operating procedures and controls relating to learning systems and digital resources.
* Ensure that learning technologies and digital processes comply with applicable WH and NHG policies, including cybersecurity, data protection, records management, procurement and financial requirements.
* Coordinate role-based access reviews and ensure appropriate segregation of duties.
* Maintain system, process, vendor, subscription and project documentation in an audit-ready manner.
* Support internal and external audits and follow through on findings and improvement actions.
* Conduct periodic reviews of system and process risks, document mitigating controls and escalate material concerns.
* Ensure that changes to learning systems and related processes are appropriately assessed, approved, tested, documented and communicated.
* Maintain business-continuity and knowledge-transfer documentation for critical learning-system processes.
  

* Stakeholder, Vendor and Project Management

* Build effective working relationships with internal users, Nursing Education, clinical services, Allied Health teams, programme owners, department learning partners, IT teams, NHG system owners and external vendors.
* Represent WH’s operational requirements and interests in institution- and cluster-level workgroups.
* Lead or coordinate learning-system, digital-resource and process-improvement projects from requirements gathering through implementation and post-implementation review.
* Develop project plans, milestones, resource requirements, risk logs and status reports.
* Coordinate vendors and internal stakeholders to ensure that deliverables, issues and dependencies are managed appropriately.
* Monitor vendor service performance and escalate material service, quality or contractual issues.
* Prepare management updates, papers and presentations on significant systems, resource and digital-improvement matters.
* Provide functional guidance to operational staff supporting LMS administration, learning records, testing or user support.
  

* Departmental Operations and Fixed Assets

* Act as the designated responsible party and departmental coordinator for P&OD’s fixed assets.
* Maintain an accurate departmental asset register and ensure that asset records are updated when equipment is received, assigned, transferred, relocated, replaced or disposed of.
* Coordinate periodic and annual fixed-asset verification exercises in accordance with WH requirements.
* Verify asset existence, location, custodian and asset-tag information and reconcile discrepancies with relevant records.
* Work with Finance, Procurement, Facilities, IT and departmental asset custodians to resolve discrepancies and complete required documentation.
* Coordinate reporting for missing, damaged, transferred, obsolete or unserviceable assets and support approved disposal or write-off processes.
* Maintain supporting records and evidence for fixed-asset verification and audit purposes.
* Ensure that asset movement and handover arrangements are documented when staff join, transfer or leave P&OD.
* Support other departmental operational, procurement, inventory or administrative responsibilities as assigned.
  

*General*

  

* Support projects under the department’s responsibility and undertake related work in collaboration with internal and external stakeholders.

* Work hand-in-hand with the P&OD team to contribute to cross-team projects or organisation-wide projects.

title: Associate Medical Director, AMEA
description:
**Company Description**

Guardant Health is a leading precision oncology company focused on guarding wellness and giving every person more time free from cancer. Founded in 2012, Guardant® is transforming patient care and accelerating new cancer therapies by providing critical insights into what drives disease through its advanced blood and tissue tests, real-world data and AI analytics. Guardant tests help improve outcomes across all stages of care, including screening to find cancer early, monitoring for recurrence in early-stage cancer, and treatment selection for patients with advanced cancer. For more information, visit guardanthealth.com and follow the company on LinkedIn , X (Twitter) and Facebook .

**About the role:**

The Associate Medical Director, AMEA will lead the development and execution of medical affairs initiatives to support the appropriate clinical adoption of Guardant products across AMEA, with a particular focus on MRD assays in ROA (Rest of AMEA, excluding Japan). The role will advance scientific understanding, address clinical evidence gaps and build confidence in the clinical value of Guardant products among healthcare professionals, payers and internal stakeholders.

Working closely with the AMEA Medical Head and cross-functional teams, the Associate Medical Director will drive scientific engagement, medical education and evidence generation aligned with regional priorities and corporate objectives. The role will also provide medical expertise to support clinical report interpretation, regulatory and reimbursement activities, and business development, while upholding patient interests and applicable ethical and compliance standards.

  

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Develop and execute regional medical plans, prioritizing early cancer detection and screening solutions, scientific education and evidence generation to support Guardant products, particularly MRD essays.
* Identify and build collaborative relationships with leading disease area experts, academic physicians and clinical centers. Prioritize engagement with influential researchers, scientific committee leaders and relevant treatment and diagnostic guideline committee members.
* Develop, review and update educational materials using current scientific evidence. Engage external experts in scientific forums, advisory discussions, institutional meetings and continuing medical education activities for academic and community healthcare professionals.
* Identify clinical evidence gaps and support company-sponsored and investigator-sponsored research aligned with medical strategy. Develop or review study concepts and collaborate with investigators and Medical Affairs colleagues to optimize study design.
* Coordinate the internal review of investigator-sponsored research proposals and facilitate approved projects. Monitor study enrolment, milestones and timelines; communicate emerging findings and implement risk mitigation plans when needed.
* Interpret research findings and support the analysis, development and review of abstracts, posters, presentations and manuscripts. Communicate relevant data through publications, congresses and regional or national educational activities.
* Collaborate with Client Services to help healthcare professionals appropriately interpret clinical reports generated by Guardant products and understand their clinical contexts.
* Train Medical Affairs colleagues, other employees and distributors on relevant clinical evidence, product information, processes and policies. Build scientific knowledge and presentation capability across the teams.
* Serve as a clinical resource for Commercial and Marketing teams through medical updates, scientific presentations and journal discussions. Provide medical input for regulatory, reimbursement and business development activities, and critically review promotional materials for scientific accuracy and balance.
Put patients first and ensure medical activities and company-sponsored or supported research meet applicable ethical, regulatory and compliance requirements. Undertake additional regional medical responsibilities assigned by the AMEA Medical Head.  

  

**Qualifications & Requirements:**

* Medical degree with oncology experience, or a PhD in an oncology-related research field.
* Minimum 8+ years of experience in oncology medical affairs.
* Clinical expertise or related experience in oncology or genetics is highly desirable.
* Demonstrated ability to build productive scientific relationships with experts at academic medical centers.
* Ability to critically evaluate scientific evidence and communicate complex clinical information clearly to medical and non-medical audiences.
* Strong collaboration skills, with the ability to work across functions and contribute at both strategic and operational levels.
* Strong problem-solving, organizational and time-management skills, with attention to detail and a proactive approach.
Excellent interpersonal skills and verbal and written communication skills in English.  

  

**AI & Digital Fluency**

Demonstrate curiosity, sound judgment, and the ability to critically evaluate and responsibly leverage AI-enabled tools in accordance with company policies, ethical standards, and regulatory requirements to improve the efficiency, effectiveness, and quality of work.  

  
  

*Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including, but not limited to, job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. If you are selected to move forward, the recruiting team will provide details specific to the factors above.*

  

*Employee may be required to lift routine office supplies and use office equipment. Majority of the work is performed in a desk/office environment; however, there may be exposure to high noise levels, fumes, and biohazard material in the laboratory environment. Ability to sit for extended periods of time.*

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability.*

Assists in carrying out the daily activities of the Human Resource Office including recruitment, total compensation, and training and development. Additionally, he/she assists in delivering HR services that meet or exceed the needs of employees and enable business success; as well as ensuring compliance with all applicable laws, regulations and operating procedures.
  
  
CANDIDATE PROFILE
  
  
Education and Experience

OR
  
  

* 2-year degree from an accredited university in Human Resources, Business Administration, or related major; no work experience required.

Assisting in Administering and Educating Employee Benefits

Assisting in Managing Employee Development

* Assists with ensuring departmental orientation processes are in place and employees receive the appropriate new hire training to successfully perform their job.

Assisting in Maintaining Employee Relations
  
  

* Assists in maintaining effective employee communication channels in the property (e.g., develops daily communications and assists with regularly scheduled property-wide meetings).

* Ensures employee issues are referred to the Department Manager for resolution or escalated to the Director of Human Resources/Multi-Property Director of Human Resources.

title: Deputy Head, Representation & Law Reform
description:
The Law Society of Singapore is seeking an experienced and driven professional to join its Representation & Law Reform Department as Deputy Head.
  
  
In this leadership role, you will help drive the Law Society's efforts in legal policy, professional practice, law reform and advocacy. You will work closely with the Council, committees, regulators, government agencies, the judiciary and members of the profession to develop policy positions, advance law reform initiatives and address issues affecting legal practice in Singapore.
  
  
This is an exceptional opportunity for a legally trained professional who is passionate about public policy, professional standards and the development of the legal profession.
  
  
Key Responsibilities
  
  
Policy Development and Law Reform
  
  
Lead and support law reform, legislative review and policy development initiatives affecting the legal profession.
  
  
Develop and articulate the Law Society's positions on policy and law reform matters.
  
  
Prepare consultation responses, policy papers, reports and submissions to government agencies, courts and other stakeholders.
  
  
Monitor and analyse legal, regulatory and industry developments that may impact legal practice and the profession.
  
  
Professional Practice and Advisory Work
  
  
Advise on legal policy and practice-related issues.
  
  
Support the Law Society's committees and working groups in addressing emerging professional and practice concerns.
  
  
Identify and evaluate trends, opportunities and risks affecting the future of legal services and legal practice.
  
  
Advocacy and Stakeholder Engagement
  
  
Build and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders across the legal ecosystem.
  
  
Represent the Law Society at meetings, consultations, forums and professional engagements.
  
  
Work collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders to advance strategic initiatives and professional interests.
  
  
Leadership and Governance
  
  
Support the Head of Department in setting strategic priorities and delivering departmental objectives.
  
  
Provide leadership and guidance to team members across policy, law reform and committee-related work.
  
  
Oversee the work of practice committees, ensuring effective governance, implementation and follow-through of decisions.
  
  
Requirements
  
  
Qualified lawyer with at least 10 years of relevant experience in legal policy and law reform work, including policy development, legislative review, stakeholder engagement, and the preparation of policy papers, consultation responses or legislative proposals.
  
  
Demonstrated experience in analysing and addressing complex legal, regulatory or professional practice issues.
  
  
Strong interest or experience in professional regulation, professional ethics, public policy or public sector legal work.
  
  
Excellent legal research, analytical, drafting and communication skills.
  
  
Demonstrated ability to engage effectively with senior stakeholders, including government agencies, regulators, the judiciary, professional bodies and industry partners.
  
  
Proven leadership, management and interpersonal skills.
  
  
Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality work in a dynamic environment.
  
  
What We Offer
  
  
A unique opportunity to influence the development of the legal profession and legal policy in Singapore.
  
  
Exposure to high-level engagement with the Bench, Bar, government agencies and key stakeholders.
  
  
Meaningful and intellectually stimulating work with a direct impact on the profession.
  
  
A collaborative and purpose-driven work environment committed to excellence and public service.
  
  
The Law Society was established under the Legal Profession Act in 1967. It carries out various statutory functions, including:
  
  
Representing, protecting and assisting members of the legal profession in Singapore; promoting in any manner the Society thinks fit the interests of the legal profession in Singapore; and
  
  
Facilitating the acquisition of legal knowledge by members of the legal profession
  
  
Maintaining and improving the standards of conduct and learning of the legal profession in Singapore
  
  
Protecting and assisting the public in all matters ancillary or incidental to the law.
  
  
Every Singapore lawyer who has in force a practising certificate is automatically a member of the Law Society. Certain categories of foreign lawyers registered with the
  
  
Legal Services Regulatory Authority
  
  
are also automatically members of the Law Society.
  
  
The mission of the Law Society is to serve its members and the public by sustaining an independent bar which upholds the rule of law and ensures access to justice. As part of its mission in ensuring access to justice for the needy, the Law Society has established a
  
  
Pro Bono Services Office
  
  
.
  
  
The Council of the Law Society, which consists of 5 statutory members and elected members, manages the affairs of the Law Society and ensures the proper performance of its functions under the Legal Profession Act.

description:

**About Us**
------------

**NTUC Health Co-operative Limited (NTUC Health)** is an NTUC enterprise that provides a comprehensive and integrated suite of quality and accessible health and eldercare services to meet the growing needs of families and their dependents. Building on close to three decades of experience and expertise, NTUC Health is among the largest providers of active ageing, senior day care, nursing home, and home personal care services in Singapore. We also serve vulnerable seniors in selected areas in Singapore through Community Case Management Services (CCMS), CREST mental health support, and a sheltered senior group home. In addition, we run a family medicine clinic.

Our purpose is to achieve ‘health for life’; enabling healthy and fulfilling years by being a trusted partner of seniors and their families in our community.

For more information, please visit ntuchealth.sg or follow us on Facebook, Instagram, and LinkedIn.
  
  
**Services:** Senior Day Care | Home Care | Nursing Home | Active Ageing and Senior Fitness | Rehabilitation and Physiotherapy | Family Medicine

**Community Support:** CCMS (Community Case Management Services) | CREST (Community Resource, Engagement and Support Team) | Henderson Home

**Job Description**
-------------------

We are looking for a strategic, hands-on WSH Manager to lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the organisation’s Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) framework across NTUC Health HQ office and operational business units. Reporting to the Head of Risk Management, you will lead and partner closely with business unit stakeholders and senior leadership to drive workplace safety and health excellence and employee well-being in full compliance with MOM, MOH, and other applicable national standards and legal requirements.

You will be working on:

**Strategy, Governance & Advisory**

* **WSH Strategy & Roadmap:** Define and execute the organization’s WSH strategy and roadmap, ensuring full alignment with applicable national regulations and industry standards (e.g., WSH Act, Fire Safety Act, ISO, and bizSAFE).
* **Policy Development & Advisory:** Develop, review, and govern organization-wide WSH policies; serve as the subject-matter expert guiding stakeholders on legal standards, codes of practice, and regulatory updates.
* **Innovation and digital transformation:** Drive digital transformation across WSH by evaluating emerging safety technologies, executing pilots, and scaling solutions to boost assurance and operational efficiency.
* **Committee Secretariat:** Act as Secretariat for the WSH and Prevention of Abuse & Harassment (PAH) Committees, facilitating end-to-end committee operations and delivering data-driven performance reports to the committees in accordance with the Terms of Reference (TOR).

**Assurance, Risk & Infrastructure Oversight**

* **Audit & Assurance Program:** Plan and execute a risk-based WSH audit program across NTUC Health, leading business unit safety representatives to evaluate effectiveness of WSH management system and critical controls.
* **Facilities & Contractor Risk:** Partner with Facilities Management team to provide centralized WSH risk oversight for new center setups, renovations, and maintenance works, contractor and subcontractor safety management.

**Incident Management & Staff Protection**

* **Incident Governance & Response:** Lead organization-wide WSH incident review and response protocols, acting as the primary liaison to law enforcement and regulatory authorities during critical events.
* **Anti-Abuse & Harassment Protocols:** Establish and enforce organisation-wide policies to prevent, manage, and respond to verbal, emotional, and physical abuse or harassment directed at staff by clients and/or next-of-kin (NOK).

**Culture & Capability Building**

* **Training & Awareness Initiatives:** Drive organisation-wide safety training, zero-harm initiatives, and WSH campaigns to cultivate a proactive, sustainable safety culture across NTUC Health.

**Job Description (Continued)**
-------------------------------

**Qualification**
-----------------

You should:

* Hold a Bachelor’s degree in any discipline.
* Have a minimum of 5 years of relevant WSH experience, specifically in managing healthcare facilities
* Have a deep understanding of building codes, fire safety systems, WSH standards, and emergency preparedness frameworks
* Hold expertise in hazard identification, risk assessment (including infection control), and compliance risk management.
* Possess a sound working knowledge of Google Workspace, Microsoft Office, and Adobe Acrobat for document creation and data manipulation
* Proficiency in data analytics (highly advantageous) to identify trends and report on safety performance
* Be a strategic and independent leader who:
  + Is a self-starter who works well under pressure and requires minimal supervision
  + possesses strong critical thinking skills, allowing you to align infrastructure and business processes with institutional safety outcomes.
  + Is experienced in change management, capable of leading the organisation through safety initiatives and operational improvement
* Be a collaborative communicator who:
  + Is an expert at engaging stakeholders, from senior management to operational frontline staff, and can bridge the gap between safety requirements and business needs.
  + Demonstrates excellent written and verbal communication skills, essential for drafting reports, presenting to committees, and managing external investigators.
* Be an organized and detail-oriented professional who:
  + Is capable of multitasking across multiple projects (such as renovations and setup) while maintaining rigorous administrative and safety documentation.
  + Brings a "solution-oriented" mindset to every challenge, ensuring that WSH compliance is achieved without sacrificing operational efficiency

**Other Information**
---------------------

It will be great if you are:

* Have a MOM-registered Workplace Safety & Health Officer (WSHO) Certificate
* SCDF-registered Fire Safety Manager (FSM).
* WSQ Advanced Certificate in Workplace Safety & Health (Level 2).
* Relevant experience in the healthcare industry and service quality operations will be advantageous.

d) Identify service gaps, emerging social trends, and community needs to inform programme development and improve the effectiveness of social service interventions.

e) Manage stakeholder engagement, communications, and feedback to foster strong relationships, gather insights, and drive continuous improvement in programmes and services.

f) Represent AMP in external engagements, sector discussions, and collaborative initiatives to promote AMP’s interests, contribute to sector development, and strengthen partnerships across the social service ecosystem.

**2. Planning, Theory of Change (ToC) and Programme Development**

a) Develop and review the division’s strategic direction, ToC, programme framework, and implementation plans to ensure alignment with AMP’s mission, strategic priorities, and community needs.

b) Translate strategic objectives and desired outcomes into clear programme priorities, service models, and operational initiatives that deliver measurable outcomes for clients.

c) Identify emerging social trends, community needs, and service gaps to inform programme development, resource allocation, and service enhancement.

d) Establish priorities for programme implementation and service delivery, taking into consideration organisational capacity, stakeholder needs, available resources, and opportunities for impact.

e) Drive monitoring and evaluation of programme effectiveness and initiatives against intended outcomes and ToC, and drive continuous improvement to enhance service quality, operational efficiency, and client outcomes.

f) Work closely with internal and external stakeholders to align strategies, strengthen service integration and ToC and advance AMP’s long-term social impact objectives.

g) Provide recommendations to Senior Management and the Board on programme development, sector trends, and policy changes.

h) Steward divisional performance and service delivery to achieve strategic objectives and advance AMP’s mission and vision.

**3. Demonstrate Corporate Governance**

a) Establish and oversee programme governance, quality assurance, risk management, and compliance frameworks to ensure effective oversight, regulatory compliance, and alignment with organisational and funding requirements.

b) Drive and strengthen the division’s audit, controls, and assurance framework to uphold accountability, mitigate operational risks, and ensureadherence to organisational policies, regulatory standards, and governancerequirements.

**4. Manage Resources**

a) Lead strategic resource planning and allocation across programmes and functions to optimise organisational effectiveness and address evolving operational priorities.

b) Establish and oversee volunteer management frameworks, policies, and practices to strengthen volunteer engagement, governance, and programme delivery capabilities.

c) Drive infrastructure, systems, and resource planning initiatives to support the division’s current operational requirements and future growthneeds.

d) Oversee resource utilisation and capacity planning to ensure sustainable service delivery and optimal deployment of organisational resources.

e) Review and approve funding proposals, business cases, and resource investments to ensure alignment with strategic priorities, operational needs, and desired organisational outcomes.

**5. Develop Organisational Capability for Service Delivery**

a) Drive capability development strategies to strengthen the division’s professional competencies, leadership bench strength, and service delivery capabilities.

b) Assess current and future workforce capability requirements and establish capability-building priorities to support the division’s strategic objectives and evolving service needs.

c) Lead the development and implementation of learning, talent, and succession plans to ensure organisational readiness and sustainability.

d) Cultivate a high-performance and continuous learning culture that promotes professional excellence, innovation, and service effectiveness.

e) Strengthen leadership and management capabilities across the division to enhance organisational resilience, employee engagement, and operational performance.

f) Champion workforce planning and talent development initiatives to ensure the division is equipped with the skills and expertise required to meet current and future service demands.

**SECONDARY DUTIES**

a) Participate in inter-divisional project committees and render support to other department events as and when required.

**REQUIREMENTS**

* Minimum 10 years of progressive leadership experience in the social service or related sector.

* Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field; postgraduate qualifications are an advantage.

* Proven track record in leading programme portfolios, service delivery, stakeholder engagement, and organisational initiatives.

* Experience in developing, implementing, and evaluating programmes that deliver measurable outcomes and community impact.

* Experience working with government agencies, community partners, funders, volunteers, and other key stakeholders.

title: Compliance Counsel
description:
**Company Description**

**About Bosch Group**

The Bosch Group is a leading global supplier of technology and services. It employs roughly 418,000 associates worldwide. The company generated sales of 90.3 billion euros in 2024. Its operations are divided into four business sectors: Mobility, Industrial Technology, Consumer Goods, and Energy and Building Technology. With technology that is “Invented for life,” Bosch wants to help improve quality of life and conserve natural resources. The Bosch Group comprises Robert Bosch GmbH and its roughly 490 subsidiary and regional companies in over 60 countries. At 136 locations across the globe, Bosch employs some 87,000 associates in research and development.

**About Robert Bosch (South East Asia)**

As the Bosch Group's regional headquarters in Singapore for Southeast Asia, Robert Bosch (South East Asia) Pte Ltd has represented the Group's interests across the region since 1923. With diversified businesses in Mobility Aftermarket, Industrial Technology, Consumer Goods, and Building Technology. Robert Bosch (SEA) Pte Ltd includes the Asia Pacific headquarters for Mobility Aftermarket, Building Technology, and Industrial Technology, as well as the Southeast Asia R&D setup for Corporate Research, Advance Engineering Centre, and Bosch Business Innovations, Bosch's in-house innovation and startup incubation network. At Bosch, we are committed through our EVP ensuring all our associates to **GROW**, **ENJOY** and **INSPIRE** during their journey with us.

 **Job Description**

**Role Overview**

We are seeking a motivated and skilled **Compliance Counsel** to join our Southeast Asia & Oceania Compliance team. In this role, you will partner closely with our **Regional Head of Corporate Compliance (based in Singapore)** to strengthen and support the compliance program of a **German-based Global 500 organization** — with a strong emphasis on **anti-bribery and anti-corruption, anti-money laundering and anti-fraud.**

The duties include mitigating risks, conducting investigations of potential violations, reviewing proposed promotion and sales incentives, overseeing training and awareness programs, developing and maintaining anti-bribery policies, monitoring and reporting the results of the compliance efforts, and providing guidance to management and employees. The ideal candidate will have a high degree of professional ethics, be assertive with strong communication skills, and is an independent, team-oriented individual who can collaborate effectively.

This is a unique opportunity for someone who thrives in a dynamic, multinational environment and wants to make a real impact on corporate integrity and governance across the region.

**What you will do (Key Responsibilities)**

**1.** **Advice and Governance**

* Provide compliance and organizational advice to management and associates on compliance topics, with a focus on anti-bribery and anti-corruption, anti-money laundering and anti-fraud.
* Understand, and keep abreast of changes to, relevant local laws and regulations.
* Implement local policies, guidelines, and procedures.
* Support further development of the compliance management program.
* Cooperate and liaise with government authorities and where necessary, instruct and manage external legal counsel
* Reporting to necessary stakeholders

**2. Internal Investigations**

* Conduct internal investigations in potential violations of internal regulations or external laws (for e.g. in areas relating to bribery, fraud, conflicts of interest), which includes report intake, case management, e-forensics, reporting, recommending appropriate sanctions, disciplinary measures, or other consequences, and, if necessary, supporting implementation of sanctions and measures.
* Collaborate with other departments, including HR, Audit and Legal, and external counsel, where required.

**3. Risk Management**

* Identify and analyse compliance risks, with a focus on anti-corruption and anti-bribery, anti-money laundering and anti-fraud, across all operations and business divisions within the region.
* Support to implement measures to monitor and mitigate risks, for example due diligence, business partner screening, internal controls and policies, risk assessments and audits.
* Review and monitor the ABC compliance management program to ensure it meets the requirements of local laws and standards, and the program maintains its effectiveness.

**4. Training & Communication**

* Implement and conduct trainings and communication activities to ensure awareness on the compliance organisation, and the organisation’s culture of compliance and ethical behavior.
* Promote speak up culture, as well as a strong culture of integrity and compliance.

**5. General**

* Undertake duties as and when assigned by Regional Head of Corporate Compliance.

  
**Qualifications**

**What We’re Looking For (Qualifications & Skills)**

* Degree in Law, Accountancy, or related fields from a recognised university.
* Minimum 8 to 10 years of experience in relevant legal compliance and ethics, internal investigations, and/or audit, within a a multinational company, law firm and/or consulting firm.
* Sound knowledge of related laws and frameworks.
* Experience with Australia and/or New Zealand is an advantage.
* Outstanding written and verbal communication skills in English. Fluency in another local language is an advantage.
* Excellent integrity and value-driven.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
* Solid time management and organizational skills. Ability to work under pressure and to manage multiple tasks in a dynamic corporate environment.
* Robust personality, excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with ability to communicate professionally with all levels within the organization.
* Self-starter and exhibits confidence and comfort with decision making, including disagreement with other stakeholders.
* Ability to work independently while being an integral part of a global, collaborative team.
* Willingness to travel.

  
**Additional Information**

**What’s In It for You**

We don’t just offer jobs—we build careers. At Bosch, you’ll benefit from:

* ️ **Flexible working hours**
* **Continuous learning**
* **Career mobility** across functions and regions
* + ️ **Well-being support** and employee assistance programs
* **Attractive compensation** including bonus schemes and insurance
* **Inclusive culture** built on respect, collaboration, and empowerment

**Next Steps**

Our recruitment process typically includes:

* Application screening
* Interview(s) with Hiring Manager, Business Leaders and HR
* Business case or technical assessment (where relevant)

title: Regulatory Compliance Manager
description:
**Your role**  
  
  
  
  
  
**What you'll be doing**  
  
  
  
  
  
**What We Need**  
  
  
  
  
  
Corpay Cross Border is a leading provider of international payments and foreign exchange solutions, supporting corporate clients operating across global markets. In Singapore, the business operates payments and FX derivatives activities under its Monetary Authority of Singapore regulatory permissions. As we continue to grow across the APAC region, we're looking for an experienced Regulatory Compliance Manager to strengthen our regulatory framework across Singapore.  
  
  
  
  
  
This is a senior, hands-on advisory role. The Regulatory Compliance Manager is the dedicated second-line regulatory compliance lead for the Singapore business. The role provides practical oversight, advice and challenge to ensure the business meets its obligations under the Payment Services Act, the Securities and Futures Act, applicable MAS notices and guidelines, and relevant corporate obligations. This role covers the full regulatory lifecycle, from interpreting new requirements and advising on business change through to monitoring, issue management, remediation and regulatory engagement. It has responsibility for the controls supporting payments, FX forwards and options, customer classification, conduct, conflicts management, incident management and trade reporting. This role reports directly to Head of Regulatory Compliance.  
  
  
  
  
  
This is an opportunity to have meaningful influence in a growing, internationally connected business. You will work closely with senior stakeholders, contribute to commercially important product and expansion decisions, and build regulatory solutions that protect customers and enable responsible growth. If you are a technically strong, commercially pragmatic compliance professional who is comfortable operating with pace and ambiguity, we would love to hear from you.  
  
  
  
  
  
**How We Work**  
  
  
  
  
  
As the Regulatory Compliance Manager, you will be expected to work in a hybrid environment. Corpay will set you up for success by providing:

  
* Assigned workspace in the Singapore office
  
  

  

  
* Company-issued equipment
  
  

  
  
  
**Role Responsibilities**  
  
  
  
  
  
There key areas of focus are:  
  
  
  
  
  
**Regulatory advice & interpretation**  
  
  
  
  
  

  
* Act as the primary regulatory compliance adviser to Singapore management and APAC control functions on MAS requirements relevant to the business.
  
  
* Interpret regulatory developments and assess their impact on the Singapore business, products, customers, systems and operating model.
  
  
* Maintain a clear, current view of the obligations applying to the Singapore entity and ensure these are reflected in the regulatory obligations register, policies, procedures and control framework.
  
  
* Provide timely, practical compliance advice on payments, FX spot, forwards, options and related customer lifecycle activities.
  
  
* Support product, distribution, outsourcing, technology and other material change assessments, including licensing-perimeter, conduct and disclosure considerations.
  
  

  
  
  
**Licensing, corporate & MAS obligations**  
  
  
  
  
  

  
* Oversee compliance with obligations connected to the Singapore payments and capital markets licences, including applicable conditions, notifications, returns, record-keeping and governance requirements.
  
  
* Coordinate the compliance input to MAS regulatory filings, responses, attestations, notifications and information requests, ensuring they are complete, accurate and submitted on time.
  
  
* Oversee the regulatory aspects of corporate compliance obligations for the Singapore entity, working with Finance, Legal, Company Secretariat and other stakeholders as needed.
  
  
* Support senior management and Board reporting on regulatory compliance matters, including key risks, breaches, open issues, remediation progress and regulatory developments.
  
  
* Maintain constructive, professional engagement with MAS and support inspections, thematic reviews and other supervisory interactions.
  
  

  
  
  
**Compliance monitoring & assurance**  
  
  
  
  
  

  
* Develop, maintain and execute a risk-based Singapore compliance monitoring plan covering key payment services and FX derivatives obligations.
  
  
* Perform thematic reviews and control testing, document outcomes clearly and agree practical corrective actions with accountable business owners.
  
  
* Track remediation through to completion, test the effectiveness of completed actions and escalate overdue or ineffective remediation.
  
  
* Use management information, customer outcomes, operational incidents and complaints to identify emerging conduct and compliance risks.
  
  

  
  
  
**Trade reporting ®gulatory data**  
  
  
  
  
  

  
* Oversee compliance with applicable Singapore trade reporting obligations for OTC derivatives, including governance over report completeness, accuracy, timeliness, reconciliations, exceptions and remediation.
  
  
* Challenge the effectiveness of data lineage, reporting controls and issue management, working closely with Operations, Technology, Trading and external reporting providers.
  
  
* Support investigations into reporting errors or other data quality issues and ensure appropriate regulatory assessment, correction and root-cause remediation.
  
  

  
  
  
**Incidents, breaches ®gulatory change**  
  
  
  
  
  

  
* Lead or support the compliance assessment of incidents, complaints, control failures and potential breaches, including impact assessment, root cause analysis and remediation planning.
  
  
* Determine, with appropriate internal and external input, whether MAS notification or other regulatory action is required and support the preparation of any notification.
  
  
* Maintain a clear record of compliance incidents and breaches and ensure management has visibility of material matters, trends and overdue actions.
  
  
* Support delivery of targeted compliance training and communications for Singapore staff and relevant regional teams.
  
  

  
  
  
**Qualifications & Skills**  
  
  
  
  
  

  
* At least five years' regulatory compliance, legal, risk or audit experience in Singapore financial services.
  
  

  

  
* Strong working knowledge of the Payment Services Act, Securities and Futures Act and relevant MAS notices, guidelines and regulatory expectations.
  
  

  

  
* Experience supporting payment services, FX, OTC derivatives, capital markets services or a comparable regulated financial services business.
  
  

  

  
* A proven ability to translate regulatory requirements into operational frameworks, controls, policies and procedures.
  
  

  

  
* Experience supporting regulatory engagement, responding to regulatory reviews or preparing submissions.
  
  

  

  
* Excellent regulatory writing, policy-drafting, analytical and stakeholder-management skills.
  
  

  

  
* The confidence to work independently, make sound risk-based judgements and explain complex issues clearly to non-specialists.
  
  

  
  
  
**It would be great if you also have**  
  
  
  
  
  

  
* Experience with MAS OTC derivatives trade reporting requirements and regulatory reporting governance.
  
  

  

  
* Experience with accredited investor and institutional investor classification, customer disclosures and suitability requirements.
  
  

  

  
* Working knowledge of AML and counter-terrorism financing controls, technology risk management expectations or outsourcing governance.
  
  

  

  
* Experience in a cross-border payments, foreign exchange or non-bank financial institution environment.
  
  

  

  
* Relevant legal, compliance, risk, audit or financial services qualification.
